description:

title: Restocking POST: O(n^2) duplicate check on unbounded list can hang the API
description:
server/main.py:190 `items: List[RestockingOrderLine] = Field(min_length=1)` has no max. server/main.py:322 runs `skus.count(s)` inside a set comprehension. list.count is a C loop holding the GIL, so one large request stalls the event loop and every other request.

Fix:
- Find duplicates with collections.Counter.
- max_length on items (len(demand_forecasts) or 100) and on sku (32 or regex).
- Run the unknown-SKU check before the duplicate check.
- pytest: a 10k-line body returns 422 quickly.

Audit ids: SEC-3, PERF-6. Effort: S

Line numbers as of main @ 5a7780c. Source: three-lens audit (Security / Performance / UX), 2026-11-12.

title: Lock down network exposure: pinned CORS origins, loopback bind, Vite /api proxy
description:
server/main.py:78-81 `allow_origins=["*"]`, `allow_credentials=True`, methods and headers `*`. server/main.py:614 binds `0.0.0.0`. client/src/api.js:3 hard-codes http://localhost:8001/api; no proxy in vite.config.js.

Fix:
- Allowed origins from env, default http://localhost:3000; allow_credentials=False.
- Methods GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE only (tasks need PATCH/DELETE); headers Content-Type only.
- Bind 127.0.0.1 by default with a HOST env override.
- Vite server.proxy for /api; API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? '/api'.
- Test: Origin https://evil.example gets no ACAO header.

Removes remote reach for the restocking DoS, input bounds and auth issues at once. Audit ids: SEC-1, SEC-5, SEC-8. Effort: S

title: Resolve the on-screen scheme into a data-scheme attribute
description:
light-dark() can theme colours but not fonts, shapes or motion, and dark mode can come from the OS or an explicit choice, so every terminal rule would otherwise need a media-query copy plus a [data-theme] copy.

Add data-scheme="dark|light" on <html> = the scheme actually on screen:
- client/index.html pre-paint script resolves explicit choice, else prefers-color-scheme.
- client/src/composables/useTheme.js keeps it in sync on choice change and on OS change (matchMedia listener).
All terminal rules then use one selector, :root[data-scheme='dark'].
close_reason: data-scheme set pre-paint in client/index.html and kept in sync by useTheme.js (choice + matchMedia listener). Verified: data-scheme=dark under OS dark, light under OS light; every terminal rule uses the single :root[data-scheme='dark'] selector.
